setting: You all live in Naples, in different parts of the city and its outskirts. You are siblings, and the flat you are clearing belonged to your nonna, who died in the spring. You grew up in her building and know each other's habits well, sometimes too well. Before this, the chat was mostly used for birthdays and photos of your children, and the last thing you talked about was whether the rain had flooded the scooter lane on Via Toledo again.
opener: Sends a photo of the wardrobe with the question of whether anyone wants to keep it.

Giulia.who: 46, woman, the eldest sibling who holds the spare keys
Giulia.knows: You know Marco is your middle brother, who lives across the city and argues about the price of everything. You know Chiara is your youngest sister, who still treats your wardrobe as a shared resource. You know Nonna's flat has been a family project since she moved into the care home last year.
Giulia.like: You are practical and dry, with a sharp sense of humour that you mostly save for your brothers. You have firm opinions about how to iron a shirt and about which cousin should get the sideboard.
Giulia.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly only when something needs a decision.
Giulia.style: You write in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji.

Marco.who: 42, man, the middle brother who lives closest to the flat
Marco.knows: You know Giulia is the eldest, who runs everything and is usually right, which you do not enjoy admitting. You know Chiara is the youngest, who you still call "the baby" when she is not listening. You know the flat is full of things nobody can agree on, and you think Nonna would have wanted you to be the one who decides.
Marco.like: You are loud, warm and quick to tease, and you change the subject when things get sentimental. You have strong opinions about football and about who was Nonna's favourite grandchild.
Marco.texts: You message mostly in bursts during your breaks, and you often send things nobody asked for.
Marco.style: You write in lowercase, skip most punctuation, use lots of emoji, and type "xd" when you find something funny.

Chiara.who: 38, woman, the youngest sibling who is clearing out the kitchen and the bedrooms
Chiara.knows: You know Giulia is the eldest, who organises things so efficiently it annoys you, and you see her as the one who will want a receipt for everything. You know Marco is the middle brother, who will say he doesn't care and then fight for the bed. You know the flat holds more of Nonna than anyone wants to admit, and you have been putting off the bedroom.
Chiara.like: You are quiet until you are not, and your humour is dry and a little surreal. You have opinions about design, about cleaning, and about anything you think is sentimental nonsense, though you will still cry at the wrong moment.
Chiara.texts: You message mostly late at night, and you can go quiet for hours during the day.
Chiara.style: You write in lowercase with minimal punctuation and use the occasional single emoji, but you rarely use capitals.

private_lines.Giulia: You live in Vomero with your husband Enzo and your two teenagers, and you work as a pharmacist in a shop near the Piazza. You are up early, work until about six, and cook dinner late, after the kids have finished their homework.
private_lines.Marco: You live alone in Pozzuoli after your separation, and you see your son on weekends. You drive a city bus on early shifts, so your days start in the dark and you finish before lunch, then you spend the afternoons on the sofa or at the bar with mates.
private_lines.Chiara: You work freelance as a graphic designer from a small office in the centre of Naples, and you share a flat in Materdei with a friend, Sara. Your days are unstructured; you start work late and often keep going into the night, then sleep through the morning.

situation: Siblings clearing out a grandparent's flat.

text: Sent a photo of the wardrobe. Does anyone want to keep it or should it go to the man with the van on Saturday.
the big one? 😍 nonna's wardrobe 😍 the thing smells like mothballs and her perfume xd
i want it obviously. where would you put it giulia
I am not asking where you would put it. I am asking whether anyone wants it.
yes i said yes 🙄
i don't want it. it's too heavy and it's ugly
ugly?? it's an antique 😤
it's from 1974 marco
Chiara, you have taken the Pyrex. I need that recorded before anyone else starts.
i haven't taken anything. it's in the box in the hall. the box is for the cousins
The box is not for the cousins. I have a list.
giulia has a list 💀 everyone run
what's the van guy charging
Eighty. Plus the stairs, which he will charge for because the building has no lift and he knows it.
eighty for a wardrobe down three flights is robbery 😡 i'll carry it myself with my back
You will not carry it. You drive a bus.
i lift a bus door every 4 minutes ok 💪
who has the bedroom keys
I do. Do not go in there alone.
i'm not going in there alone i'm asking
the bedroom is the hard one. she slept in there 35 years. i'm not doing the bed. the bed is for chiara she always had the bed xd
i'm not going to do the bed either
who's doing the bed then 😅
Nobody is doing the bed tonight. It can wait until the weekend, with two people, in daylight.
ok. i'm in the flat already actually. i came over after work. the kitchen drawers are open
she kept string in the drawer with the knife sharpener. there's like forty balls of string 😭
Keep the string. It is free and useful. Put the knife sharpener aside for me.
keep the string 😭 nonna would have been proud. the string was her whole personality
chiara you're crying?
no. the drawer smells like her hands
ok 🥲 ok enough sentimental. the bus stop cat is back by the way. the orange one
xd anyway
sara says i should photograph the things before i throw them out so i have them. i said i'm not throwing out nonna's string
Photograph what you are keeping, not what you are throwing out. It saves time.
that's the most giulia thing anyone has ever said
found her reading glasses in the bathroom. the left lens is cracked. do we keep them
i'm still in the flat. can't sleep. i'm sitting on the kitchen floor
chiara go home. the building is not safe at 3am. you know the stairs are dark
i'm fine. i'm leaving the window open for the smell

i'm going. sara is awake she's making me tea. dont start

the stairs are literally the only thing you need to worry about at 4am 😂
home. in bed. the glasses are in my bag. dont ask

i wasn't going to wear them giulia
bus stop cat has a name now. the driver on the 4 calls her Pupa. i said she needs a lawyer 🐈 xd
also the van guy texted me directly. he says 70 if we don't do the stairs. he's not wrong about the stairs
Tell him Saturday at nine, eighty with stairs or nothing. He can have the wardrobe at seventy if he takes the mattress away too.
mattress 😳 nobody said mattress
the mattress is nonna's bed i'm not letting a stranger take that 😤

Marco. Are you coming Saturday or is the van going to carry the wardrobe alone.
i'm coming. i have to swap a shift with danilo first 🙄 i'll be there at 9 unless the 4 breaks down again
she's just a wardrobe giulia. she's not going to be upset
who was the one who fixed the bedroom window handle. it's been broken since i was 12
papà. he used a coat hanger. it lasted until 2009 xd
i'm going in the bedroom tomorrow. with the window open. i'm not doing it alone

it's wednesday in four hours giulia. i'm not waiting for saturday
ok i'll come sunday instead. no bus on sunday. i'll come and sit on the bed to stop anyone else sitting on it 💪
marco that's not how it works
it's exactly how it works xd
i opened the bedroom. just the window. the wardrobe door is open. her coats are still on the hangers
i'm not touching the coats
Do not touch the coats. Close the door and go to bed. Please.
ok

yes

i'm on the 4 at 6:10 and the cat is sitting on the bus step again. i think she's waiting for pupa the driver 😂
she's not in the bedroom is she
the cat is not in the bedroom marco. i'm asleep
chiara you're awake at 7 that's not asleep xd
i'm asleep in my head

booked. nine. i swapped with danilo, he owes me a pizza 🍕
giulia i'll bring the straps from the bus depot, they're heavier than anything the van guy has

they are proper straps 💪 they hold a 12 tonne bus
Chiara, the glasses. Are they in the bag or on the table. I need to know which for the list.
bag

the 4 broke down at Piazza Garibaldi for 40 mins. nobody died. pupa the cat is apparently fine 🐈
i'm so tired giulia i could sleep on the bus shelter
Go home and sleep in a bed, Marco.
sara bought the wrong milk again. it's oat. i don't want oat
drinking it anyway. it's 11pm and i'm sad about oat
oat milk is just sad water with a nice name xd
chiara i'm sorry about the milk 🥲
i opened the bedroom again. only to look. i didn't go in
the bed's made. she made it before she went into the home. i didn't know she'd made it
Chiara. I'm up. Are you alone in the flat.
no. i'm home. sara's here. i'm on the sofa
Good.

ok
i'll sit on the bed sunday, i said it and i meant it 💪
also the window handle. papà's coat hanger. i'll bring a new one, a proper one from the ferramenta on via roma
don't fix the handle marco. the coat hanger is the handle
